Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Chiron and the Identity Wound Explained", "body": "Davin explained that Chiron was discovered in 1977 while in Aries, was reclassified several times as an asteroid, a comet and a planetoid before astronomers settled on the label centaur, and was named for the wounded healer of Greek myth. He argued that the object's struggle over classification echoed the centaur's rejection by his mother and his search for where he belonged. Davin defined identity as self-awareness plus a sense of belonging, called a blockage in either one an identity wound, and described his Chironversations series as a place for people to tell their stories."}, {"title": "Accepting the Wound Instead of Fixing It", "body": "Davin argued that Chiron's wound was never fully cured but could be accepted and worked with, and that people carrying a given wound were best placed to help others in that same area, pointing to Chiron's glyph as a key. Rachel cautioned that endless healing could become stagnation that kept people from their full potential, and Davin agreed that staying stuck was no goal. Chance described noticing his harsh inner critic give way to supportive self-talk that felt like being cheered on, and wondered aloud whether that was what people meant by guides."}, {"title": "Where the Chiron Story Came From", "body": "One participant asked how a body found in 1977 could match a myth so closely with how Chiron shows up in birth charts, and offered two explanations, that the object was known long ago or that the myth shaped the chart readings. Another participant proposed a third, that an ancient culture once held a complete view of the sky, lost it, and later rediscovered the pieces like a scavenger hunt. Davin said he did not know whether the myths placed Chiron in the sky, and the group traded references linking Chiron to Sagittarius."}, {"title": "Horses, Archers, and Symbolic Connections", "body": "Mario said the half serpent king Erichthonius was likely the figure behind the chariot card, which opened a long run on horse and rider symbolism. Rachel described a horse rune as standing for good relationship with nature and partnership, and the group compared horses, boats and chariots as symbols of journeying. Davin described the sign before Sagittarius as a stage of transformational letting go, followed by Sagittarius developing the aim before releasing the arrow. One participant argued that the Chi Rho symbol and Hebrew letter values tied Chiron to a healer and messiah archetype."}, {"title": "Art, Self Trust, and Real Stories", "body": "Davin said he had drawn since childhood, paused for long stretches, and only recently began formal study of figure drawing at 46, while sharing his work online opened new ideas about art. Chance argued that making it up as you go is what creative source does, and said trusting his intuition in tuning sessions and podcasting taught him not to feel like a fake. Davin closed by describing an open invitation for ordinary people to share real stories in a Chironversation, recalling a time before the internet when people traded stories outdoors."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Astrological analyst and artistic adept Davin Boerstler joins us tonight for a Vibe Rant! In addition to his insightful contributions to the online InnerVerse tribe and relentless encouragement to us all to make more art, on Davin's Youtube channel he has honed in on the self-healing potential our current moment in time as Chiron passes through the sign of Aries.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "An identity wound is a difficulty, a trauma, or a blockage of energy that occurred somewhere that's interfering with one of these domains, either your sense of self-awareness or your sense of belonging. And I'm always reminded of the Chiron story. And I think that this identity wound in a way, it's part of the human condition, right? As being physical creatures and spiritual creatures and walking this line.", "author": "Mario Garza", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/94a2fe35-cc60-4591-8931-7e2b7af18c82/MARIO-GARZA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "That's how powerful these myths are and why it's so important to work with them.
